newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ retail sales trend continues growth in July.
newsitem.headline: NZ retail sales trend continues growth in July.

text.p: The underlying trend in New Zealand retail sales indicated growth of 0.2 percent in July 1996, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Tuesday.
The trend had shown steady growth for the last two years, averaging four percent annually.
Seasonally-adjusted retail sales rose 2.3 percent against sales in June. Actual retail sales at NZ$3.16 billion were 4.2 percent, or $127 million, higher than a year ago.

July sales for 10 of the 15 storetypes recorded increases when compared to July 1995, with the fastest rates of growth in cafes, restaurants and takeaway outlets (up 11.9 percent); recreational goods (up 11.4 percent) and personal and household services (up 11.1 percent).
SNZ said sales may have been affected by personal tax cuts which came into effect on July 1, and the extension of the July school holidays to two weeks from one week.
Motor vehicle services contributed 30 percent, or $38 million, of the total annual rise in actual retail sales.

Other significant increases were recorded by food retailing (up $26.5 million); cafes, restaurants and takeaway outlets (up $20.9 million); and accommodation, hotels and liquor outlets (up $15.7 million).
Total new car registrations rose by 39 percent in the year to July 1996, while registrations of cars previously registered overseas rose 68 percent over the same period.
Actual retail sales, excluding both automotive storetypes, were $2.1 billion in July, 4.2 percent higher than a year ago.
Total sales in the South Island rose 4.6 percent in the year to July, while North Island sales rose four percent.
